overview: The board approved a special permit for a new BJ's fueling station and recommended a new brewery ordinance to the City Council. It also recommended a mixed-use redevelopment project at 30-36 Salem Street while declining to recommend a new historic district for 16 Foster Court.

items.title: Meeting Opening and Minutes
items.summary: Chair Andre Leroux opened the remote meeting and tabled the approval of the August 20, 2020, minutes because they were not finalized.

items.title: Special Permit: 278 Middlesex Avenue (BJ’s Gas)
items.summary: The board approved a special permit and site plan review for a self-service fueling station at 278 Middlesex Avenue, conditioned on off-site bicycle lane improvements, enhanced landscaping, and the installation of electric vehicle charging stations. The approval followed revisions by the applicant to narrow driveway widths and provide dedicated pedestrian connections to the existing wholesale club.

items.title: Brewery Zoning Ordinance
items.summary: The board voted to recommend that the City Council adopt a zoning amendment defining and regulating breweries, taprooms, and brewpubs, which would be allowed by right in most industrial and commercial districts. The board suggested adding language to explicitly allow these establishments to produce and serve food on-site.

items.title: Site Plan Review: 30-36 Salem Street
items.summary: The board voted to recommend site plan review approval to the Board of Appeals for a four-story mixed-use project involving the renovation of a historic 1915 building. The recommendation was conditioned on the applicant adding rear balconies for residential units and continuing design coordination with the Historical Commission regarding the front facade and historic marquee.

items.title: Local Historic District: 16 Foster Court
items.summary: The board voted to make no recommendation to the City Council regarding the establishment of a single-property local historic district at 16 Foster Court. While acknowledging the building's federal-era history and ties to the shipbuilding industry, board members expressed concerns regarding the owner's lack of cooperation and the potential for the structure to be relocated.

items.title: Meeting Schedule and Adjournment
items.summary: The board scheduled its next meeting for September 30, 2020, to discuss proactive planning items such as design guidelines and linkage fees before adjourning.
